name: Drake Industrial Deep-Mine Survival Suit
description:
A ruggedized suit designed for mining operations in deep subsurface environments where tunnel collapse, gas pockets, and water intrusion are constant risks. The suit incorporates an emergency rebreather, a personal locator beacon, impact-resistant plating on the torso and head, and chemical glow strips that activate if power is lost.

The Deep-Mine Suit doesn't prevent mine disasters — it keeps the wearer alive long enough for rescue. The 72-hour rebreather and locator beacon have pulled survivors from collapses that would otherwise have been body recoveries.
functionality: 72-hour survival support, impact protection, beacon location, emergency illumination
what_it_says: You work underground where the ceiling might fall, the air might poison you, and this suit is your chance of being found alive.
story_hooks: A Deep-Mine Survival Suit's locator beacon activates from a location that isn't a mine — it's under a Spire building, from a subsurface level that doesn't appear on any structural plan.

physical_description.visual_profile: A bulky, militaristic one-piece survival suit with pronounced armor plating across the torso and shoulders. The silhouette is deliberately ungainly — wide through the chest and upper arms, tapering at the wrists and ankles. A prominent helmet-integrated collar flares outward. The overall impression is industrial and utilitarian, built for function over form.
physical_description.fit: Compression-fitted through the limbs with intentional slack at joints for movement and equipment layering. The torso is structured and rigid due to reinforced panels. Designed to accommodate heavy undergarments and auxiliary breathing apparatus.
physical_description.primary_material: Heavy ballistic weave composite with embedded aramid fiber, treated synthetic leather reinforcement panels, impact-absorbing polymer plating
physical_description.texture: Rough, textured weave with raised stitching visible on seams. Impact plates feel hard and dimpled. The collar features embossed grip ridges. Chemical glow strips are smooth and recessed into the fabric.
physical_description.color_scheme: Charcoal grey base with bright safety orange accent piping along seams and around the collar. Reflective silver trim on shoulders and chest. Black impact plates. Glow strips are pale phosphorescent green when inactive.
closures: Heavy-duty magnetic snap system down the front torso
Friction-fit wrist and ankle cuffs with locking toggles
Helmet collar locks via quarter-turn bayonet fitting
distinctive_features: Integrated rebreather housing on right shoulder — cylindrical, textured, with manual activation lever
Personal locator beacon (PLB) mount on upper back with flip-up antenna housing
Reinforced impact plating on sternum, ribs, and back in raised relief pattern
Chemical glow strips running down both sides of torso and around helmet collar
Drainage ports with one-way valves at lower legs and back seam
Drake Industrial logo stamped in metallic gray on left shoulder
Emergency whistle integrated into right wrist cuff
Numbered survivor tether loops sewn into shoulder and hip seams
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 4 — working class heavy-duty equipment. Expensive but not luxury; purchased by mining corporations as mandatory PPE for dangerous conditions.
physical_description.cultural_context: Marks the wearer as a subsurface laborer or rescue operative. The suit broadcasts 'danger job' and 'corporation-issued safety.' Wearing one outside of mining contexts signals either active danger or someone reliving trauma. In ungoverned zones, a used suit might indicate scavenging or prior industrial experience.
physical_description.condition_typical: Worn examples show mud caking in seams, scuffing on impact plates, faded safety piping, and frayed edges on glow strips. Survivor suits often have dents and crack patterns in the plating from actual collapses. Many are patched at stress points with athletic tape or field repairs.

image_prompt: A rugged mining worker in a Drake Industrial Deep-Mine Survival Suit, standing in a dimly-lit subsurface facility. The suit's charcoal grey and safety orange coloring is highlighted by harsh blue-white LED work lights. The integrated rebreather and locator beacon on the shoulder are in sharp focus. The character's posture is alert, ready. Chemical glow strips glow faintly green against the dark fabric. Concrete walls and mining equipment visible in the background. Moody, industrial aesthetic.
